Fits a 'JAGS' model

Source: R/JAGS-fit.R
JAGS_fit.Rd

Compiles JAGS model syntax, data, formulas and priors into a model and samples it using rjags.

JAGS_fit(
  model_syntax,
  data = NULL,
  prior_list = NULL,
  formula_list = NULL,
  formula_data_list = NULL,
  formula_prior_list = NULL,
  formula_scale_list = NULL,
  chains = 4,
  adapt = 500,
  burnin = 1000,
  sample = 4000,
  thin = 1,
  autofit = FALSE,
  autofit_control = list(max_Rhat = 1.05, min_ESS = 500, max_error = 0.01, max_SD_error =
    0.05, max_time = list(time = 60, unit = "mins"), sample_extend = 1000, restarts = 10,
    max_extend = 10, check_indicators = FALSE, monitor = NULL, burnin_max_Rhat = "auto",
    burnin_extend = 500, burnin_max_extend = 10),
  parallel = FALSE,
  cores = chains,
  silent = TRUE,
  seed = NULL,
  add_parameters = NULL,
  required_packages = NULL,
  formula_random_prior_list = NULL,
  formula_random_effects_compile_list = NULL,
  jags_modules = NULL,
  runtime_setup = NULL,
  runtime_cache = NULL,
  worker_output = NULL,
  sampler_gates = FALSE,
  sampler_blocks = NULL,
  runtime_report = NULL,
  sampler_joint = NULL,
  sampler_probabilities = NULL,
  sampler_nested_weights = FALSE,
  ...
)

JAGS_extend(
  fit,
  autofit_control = list(max_Rhat = 1.05, min_ESS = 500, max_error = 0.01, max_SD_error =
    0.05, max_time = list(time = 60, unit = "mins"), sample_extend = 1000, restarts = 10,
    max_extend = 10, check_indicators = FALSE, monitor = NULL),
  parallel = FALSE,
  cores = NULL,
  silent = TRUE,
  runtime_setup = attr(fit, "runtime_setup", exact = TRUE),
  runtime_cache = attr(fit, "runtime_cache", exact = TRUE),
  worker_output = NULL,
  adapt = NULL,
  runtime_report = attr(fit, "runtime_report", exact = TRUE)
)

Arguments

model_syntax

jags syntax for the model part

data

list containing data to fit the model (not including data for the formulas)

prior_list

named list of prior distribution (names correspond to the parameter names) of parameters not specified within the formula_list. Factor priors must carry their levels, set with prior_factor_levels().

formula_list

named list of formulas to be added to the model (names correspond to the parameter name created by each of the formula)

formula_data_list

named list of data frames containing data for each formula (names of the lists correspond to the parameter name created by each of the formula)

formula_prior_list

named list of named lists of prior distributions (names of the lists correspond to the parameter name created by each of the formula and the names of the prior distribution correspond to the parameter names) of parameters specified within the formula

formula_scale_list

named list of named lists for standardizing continuous predictors (names of the lists correspond to the parameter name created by each of the formula). Each entry should be a named list where continuous predictors with TRUE values will be standardized. Defaults to NULL (no standardization).

chains

number of chains to be run, defaults to 4

adapt

number of samples used for adapting the MCMC chains, defaults to 500. In JAGS_extend(), the number of adaptation iterations run when the backend builds the sampler from the stored chain states; the default NULL uses the setting of the initial fit. A value supplied to JAGS_extend() applies to that call only: the returned fit keeps the initial setting, which later calls without adapt use again.

burnin

number of burnin iterations of the MCMC chains, defaults to 1000. Its last iterations are checked for agreement of the chains before sampling starts, and with autofit burn-in can be extended (see burnin_max_Rhat in autofit_control); fit$burnin holds the burn-in that was run.

sample

number of draws to retain per chain, defaults to 4000. Each chain runs sample * thin sampling iterations.

thin

thinning interval for the MCMC samples, defaults to 1

autofit

whether the models should be refitted until convergence criteria specified in autofit_control. Automatic fitting stops once every diagnostic that can be assessed meets its criterion, or at max_time or max_extend. Assessability is judged from the draws available at each check. Automatic fitting does not extend a fit for diagnostics that cannot be assessed then (a mixture component or indicator state that no chain has visited, draws that are constant), so a quantity that only more draws would reveal is not waited for; every diagnostic that can be assessed still extends the fit. A fit in which nothing can be assessed stops after its initial sampling (in JAGS_extend(), after its first extension). When automatic fitting stops with diagnostics that cannot be assessed, a warning of class BayesTools_autofit_not_assessable (also BayesTools_fit_diagnostic) names them unless silent = TRUE; it is not stored in the fit's warnings attribute. Check the returned fit with JAGS_check_convergence(). Defaults to FALSE.

autofit_control

a list of arguments controlling the autofit function. Convergence thresholds and max_time$time must be finite and non-missing. Set a convergence threshold or max_time to NULL to disable that check. Possible options are:

max_Rhat

maximum R-hat error for the autofit function. Defaults to 1.05. R-hat is the larger of the point estimate and the upper confidence limit of the potential scale reduction factor, whereas the summary tables show the point estimate (see JAGS_check_convergence()).

min_ESS

minimum effective sample size. Defaults to 500.

max_error

maximum MCMC error. Defaults to 0.01.

max_SD_error

maximum MCMC error as the proportion of standard deviation of the parameters. Defaults to 0.05.

max_time

list with fields time and unit, specifying when the automatic fitting function is stopped. The unit value corresponds to the units argument of difftime.

max_extend

number of times after which the automatic fitting function is stopped.

sample_extend

number of samples between each convergence check. Defaults to 1000. With "auto", each extension is sized from the convergence check that failed, which then assesses every selected parameter: with n retained draws per chain and f the largest required growth over the parameters (min_ESS / ESS, (error / max_error)^2, and (SD_error / max_SD_error)^2 for the criteria that are set, and at least 2 for an R-hat above max_Rhat; diagnostics that are not assessable add nothing), the extension is n * (f - 1) * 1.1 draws per chain rounded up to a multiple of 100, then at most 2 * n rounded down to a multiple of 100, then at least 1000 (the minimum wins when 2 * n is smaller), and at most the largest multiple of 100 whose sampling iterations (draws times thin) stay within the backend's integer limit. With max_time, it is then at most the draws per chain that the time left allows at the rate observed so far (the time on the max_time clock divided by the retained draws per chain run since that clock started; in JAGS_fit() the clock starts before the initial run, so the rate includes its adaptation and burn-in), rounded down to a multiple of 100; when that is below 100, the fitting stops with the max_time warning. In JAGS_extend(), the first extension is sized from the check of the supplied fit and, with no rate observed yet, is not shortened. Without max_time, each extension of a fit that cannot converge multiplies the draws per chain by about 2.1 (a failed R-hat) and up to 3 (large ESS or error deficits), up to max_extend. An extension, of either kind, whose last draw would have an iteration number beyond .Machine$integer.max is not started: the fitting stops with the last fit and a warning of its own.

restarts

maximum number of fitting attempts when the model fails to initialize; every failed attempt but the last is retried with new initial values (restarts = 1 fits once, without a retry). A failed attempt that is retried is reported as a warning of the fit. Defaults to 10.

check_indicators

whether model indicator variables should be included in convergence checks, including when monitor selects a narrower parameter set. Auxiliary inclusion-probability coordinates remain excluded unless requested explicitly. Defaults to FALSE.

monitor

optional character vector selecting parameters for convergence checks. Base names select all indexed elements. Requests are resolved against the monitored nodes that the summary tables show, including the derived and auxiliary ones that the default selection excludes. Base names that are not monitored are rejected before sampling (error class BayesTools_parameter_not_found); an indexed element such as "mu[2]" is resolved against the fitted columns after the first run and fails then when it does not exist. Defaults to NULL, which checks the default selection of JAGS_check_convergence(): the sampled parameters of the priors, add_parameters that depend on a stochastic node, and the stochastic nodes that formulas monitor (such as latent random effects and LKJ primitives). Deterministic nodes that formulas monitor (such as random-effect correlation matrices and their Cholesky factors) are derived and not checked by default. The role of every fitted coordinate is stored in the convergence_role column of parameter_coordinates().

burnin_max_Rhat

the threshold of the readiness check between burn-in and sampling. Defaults to "auto", which is 1.7 + 0.9 / chains (2.15 for two chains, 2 for three, 1.925 for four); a number fixes the threshold, an omitted element takes its default, and NULL turns the check off. The check runs, also without autofit, in the initial fit of JAGS_fit() (afresh in each restart attempt; not in JAGS_extend() or the automatic extensions after sampling) when there are at least two chains, the block of the last min(burnin_extend, floor(burnin / thin)) draws of burn-in, taken every thin iterations as in sampling, has at least 100 draws, and JAGS assigns the model a sampler. The iterations of the block (its draws times thin) run with the monitors on; their draws are checked and then dropped. Each chain's block is split into halves, and the chains are ready when the point estimate of the potential scale reduction factor over the half-chains (coda::gelman.diag()) is at most burnin_max_Rhat for every quantity that the convergence check assesses (the selection of monitor and check_indicators; a requested state of an indicator, such as "mu_indicator (state 3)", that the block does not visit is not assessable there). A quantity that is constant over the half-chains, or not finite in each of them, is not assessable; one that is not finite in some half-chains only fails the check. In a model to which JAGS assigns no sampler (every node is drawn directly given its parents, as in a model without data) the chains cannot disagree, and the whole burn-in runs unmonitored, as with the check off. When the chains are not ready, a fit with autofit extends burn-in by blocks of burnin_extend draws (burnin_extend * thin iterations), each checked alone, until they are ready, burnin_max_extend blocks were added, or max_time is exceeded (checked before each block); a fit without autofit keeps its burn-in. Chains that are still not ready start sampling; a warning of class BayesTools_burnin_not_converged (also BayesTools_fit_diagnostic) is issued once that initial sampling of the attempt the fit keeps has finished (a restart attempt that is discarded warns nothing), before any automatic extension, whatever silent is, and kept in the fit's warnings attribute. When no monitored node lacks observed descendants, a fit whose chains are ready at once has the same draws, final states and samplers as with the check off: monitoring changes no sampler, but JAGS samples a monitored node without observed descendants (such as a predictive quantity) from the chain's random-number stream. The check cannot detect chains that are all in the same wrong state. The automatic value falls with the number of chains: for chains that agree but are autocorrelated, the statistic has the same typical value for any number of chains but varies less the more chains are run, so a threshold that falls with the number of chains keeps false alarms from becoming more frequent with them and keeps part of the sensitivity to one deviating chain that a fixed value loses. A slowly mixing fit can exceed the threshold although its chains agree, because the statistic grows with the autocorrelation of the block's draws; a larger thin then helps when more widely spaced draws are less correlated, while more burn-in is the remedy for chains that have not yet reached the same region. The check needs 100 draws at the fit's thinning: with burnin below 100 * thin it does not run, and when it runs with burnin at most burnin_extend * thin, the block holds every complete window of thin iterations of burn-in (the first burnin %% thin iterations run unmonitored), so raise burnin together with thin.

burnin_extend

the number of final burn-in draws, taken every thin iterations, that the readiness check assesses, and of each extension of burn-in (burnin_extend * thin iterations); at least 100. Defaults to 500. When the check runs with burnin at most burnin_extend * thin, its block holds every complete window of thin iterations of burn-in, and the first burnin %% thin iterations run unmonitored.

burnin_max_extend

the largest number of extensions of burn-in, with autofit only. Defaults to 10. An extension after which the last retained draw would have an iteration number beyond .Machine$integer.max is not run; the warning then names that limit.

parallel

whether to distribute chains over PSOCK worker processes. Defaults to FALSE, which runs all chains in the calling process. Each sampling process uses one JAGS thread.

cores

maximum number of workers when parallel = TRUE, defaults to chains.

silent

whether the function should proceed silently, defaults to TRUE

seed

seed for random number generation by JAGS_fit(): an integer between -.Machine$integer.max and .Machine$integer.max. Draws are reproducible for the same seed, chains, and R random-number generator settings (RNGkind()), and, with parallel = TRUE, the same cores and backend versions. Initial values are drawn from the priors after set.seed(seed), and each chain's JAGS random-number seed is drawn from the same seed with sample.int(.Machine$integer.max, chains) (see JAGS_get_inits). A chain's JAGS seed therefore does not depend on the number of chains, but the JAGS generator does: with more than four chains it changes from "base::Super-Duper" to "lecuyer::RngStream", so the draws of a chain differ between fits with up to four and with more chains. The chains of adjacent seeds (e.g., seed and seed + 1) do not share random-number streams. Automatic restarts after a failed initialization (see restarts in autofit_control) draw their seeds from a separate stream of the same seed (the first L'Ecuyer-CMRG substream), so the i-th restart does not repeat the fit with seed + i. A seeded fit restores the caller's random-number state (.Random.seed and RNGkind()) when it returns. With seed = NULL, the initial values are drawn from one seed taken from the caller's random-number stream (see JAGS_get_inits), which the fit then continues to use.

add_parameters

vector of additional parameter names that should be monitored but were not specified in the prior_list. Automatic fitting checks their convergence like that of the other parameters. Fully observed data and a node that the model syntax defines deterministically (<- or =) from data and constants only are structural constants and do not block convergence. A node that is stochastic (~) or depends on a stochastic node is checked, and its constant draws are not assessable (see allow_not_assessable in JAGS_check_convergence()). A name that repeats a parameter of prior_list is refused. A parameter that a formula needs monitored, such as the scalar SD source of a random-effect block (random_sd_source("tau")), is added automatically and, when prior_list already holds its prior, is monitored through that prior.

required_packages

character vector specifying list of packages containing JAGS models required for sampling (in case that the function is run in parallel or in detached R session). Defaults to NULL. Parallel workers must load the same versions and native library builds as the parent session. When developing packages with load_all(), install matching builds into a library and set R_LIBS_USER before starting R and its workers.

formula_random_prior_list

optional named list of prior_random() objects for random effects in formula_list. Required for any formula that contains random effects.

formula_random_effects_compile_list

optional named list of random_effects_compile() objects controlling which formula random-effect blocks are sampled and which are compiled as marginalized structural blocks. Defaults to NULL, which preserves the current all-sampled behavior.

jags_modules

character vector specifying JAGS modules required by the generated model syntax. Defaults to NULL.

runtime_setup

optional function accepting one context list. After required packages and JAGS modules load, it is called with phase = "start" in the calling process, then each parallel worker. The context contains role ("local", "coordinator", or "worker"), chains (total chains), processes (sampling processes), process_id (one-based worker index, or zero for the coordinator), process_chains (chains assigned to this process; zero for the coordinator), and parallel. Chains are divided round-robin among at most min(cores, chains) workers. On exit, including fitting failures, workers are stopped before the calling process receives phase = "finish" with its original topology context. Worker processes do not receive a finish callback. If stopping workers fails, a warning is issued and the finish callback is not run; cleanup still attempts every remaining worker and closes failed connections. This permits releasing coordinator resources before parallel work and restoring them afterward. Return values are ignored. The callback must be idempotent, must not change random-number generator state, and should capture only small immutable settings. Packages it uses must be included in required_packages. The callback is stored with the fit; JAGS_extend() reuses it with the current chain and worker topology. Supplying NULL explicitly disables replay.

runtime_cache

optional function accepting context and state = NULL for optional computational caches. It must not change inference targets or random-number state and must capture only small settings. After runtime setup, a fit or extension calls it with context$phase = "restore" and a list of prior process shards assigned to this process (empty for new fits or workers without an assigned shard). Each prior shard is sent to at most one current process, in round-robin order; shards are not duplicated when worker count increases. Before workers stop, a completed fit calls it with context$phase = "capture" and state = NULL. Capture returns one serializable shard, or NULL to retain no state. The fitted object's runtime_state attribute stores process shards separately from its small runtime_cache callback. Backend extension calls receive neither attribute. JAGS_extend() restores old state independently of whether its callback elects to capture fresh state. Callback warnings and errors are reported without discarding valid draws; a failed capture callback leaves a NULL shard for its process. If a worker connection fails during capture, no shard is retained from any process for that fit. Capture warnings, including such failures, are also recorded in the fit's warnings attribute. Error and interrupt cleanup does not attempt capture; ordinary runtime cleanup still runs. Retained R snapshots, serialization buffers, and the caller's old fitted object consume memory in addition to active cache storage. Callback packages must be listed in required_packages. Passing NULL disables capture and restore.

worker_output

optional file path for parallel worker stdout and stderr. The parent directory must exist. Workers append to the same file, so messages can interleave. NULL retains the backend default of discarding worker output. This setting is call-specific and is not retained with the fit; supply it again to JAGS_extend() when needed. Connection failures stop automatic fitting retries and preserve the original backend error.

sampler_gates

whether the branch parameters of a publication-bias mixture prior (a prior_mixture() of prior_none(), prior_PET(), prior_PEESE(), prior_weightfunction(), prior_phacking(), and prior_bias() branches) are declared to the gated sampler of the BayesTools JAGS module: while its branch is not selected, a parameter is drawn directly from its prior instead of by slice sampling. A branch whose nodes the model uses outside the mixture composition (in model_syntax, another prior, or a formula) is not gated. Defaults to FALSE.

sampler_blocks

optional list of character vectors of names of the combined prior list (prior_list and the formula priors). The scalar parameters of the priors of one vector are updated jointly by the factor slice sampler of the BayesTools JAGS module, which slice-samples along the principal directions of their posterior covariance learned during adaptation. A block may contain simple continuous scalar priors, treatment and independent factor priors, a single weight function, PET and PEESE priors, direct random-effect SDs and scalar correlations with simple continuous scalar priors, and the allocation SD and Dirichlet allocation weights of a random-effect variance allocation; a prior may be in one block only. A block that expands to fewer than two parameters is not declared and is recorded as declined. sampler_blocks may also be a function of one argument, the combined prior list (formula priors under their final names and with their attributes), called once by JAGS_fit(), that returns NULL or such a list. Defaults to NULL. Neither sampler_gates nor sampler_blocks changes the model or its posterior distribution, only the draws. Invalid declarations stop with an error of class BayesTools_sampler_declaration_error. The declarations are stored in attr(fit, "sampler_declarations"), which JAGS_extend() keeps: a list of the data frames gates, blocks and declined (one row per declined gate branch or block, with its kind, prior, branch or block, nodes and reason). For successful fits with gate declarations, gate_claims records the sampler assignment for each gate when the reported JAGS node can be matched. A gate whose assignment status or sampler differs across workers has status "mixed". A density that cannot be calculated (NaN) at a point the factor slice sampler evaluates stops the fit with a JAGS error, as with the stock samplers.

runtime_report

optional function accepting one context list, as for runtime_setup but with context$phase = "report", that reads small values of a process, such as sampler counters. It is called in every process that ran chains (the calling process of a serial fit, each worker of a parallel fit) after every backend run: the initial run, each restart attempt, each automatic extension, and each extension of JAGS_extend(). JASP sampling batches share one report for the initial run. An error in a JASP progress callback propagates to the caller. If warmup has completed, the reporting callback runs before the error propagates. The callback must not change inference targets or random-number state, must capture only small settings, and returns NULL or a small serializable value. The values of runs that do not give the returned fit (failed attempts and failed extensions) are dropped; the callback is still called after them, so that read-and-clear state starts the next run clean, but not after a worker connection failure. The runtime_report_values attribute of a fit is the list of the kept runs of the call, in order, each a list with one element per process (NULL elements kept in place); it is NULL when no process reported a value, and a fit that failed has none. Callback warnings and errors are signalled with the process they came from and recorded in the fit's warnings attribute when the run is kept. A callback error leaves NULL for its process; after a warning, the value is kept. A failed transport of the report leaves NULL for every process, with one warning. The callback is stored as the runtime_report attribute; JAGS_extend() reuses it and reports only its own runs (the values of the extended fit are not carried over). Callback packages must be listed in required_packages. Passing NULL disables the report.

sampler_joint

optional package callback accepting prior_list, formula_design and data. It receives the combined bound prior list, the finalized formula designs and the combined model and formula data, once before compilation. Return NULL to decline, or a list with a nonempty markers list and optional data list of named finite numeric constants that are referenced by the markers. Each marker specifies a fresh name, an ordered arguments list and one of tag or distribution. Each argument contains one or more node references (bare names or positive integer subscripts or ranges) or finite numeric literals. Multiple entries in one argument are combined with c(). References can come from the existing model and data or the callback's numeric constants. Marker names are reserved to the declarations. A tag is a registered deterministic JAGS function with a name prefixed with <lowercased-module>_ for a provider listed in jags_modules. It must return a fixed finite value for admissible arguments. Use a dedicated function without aliases. The model must reserve that function for tags to prevent JAGS from reusing a scientific node. The tag creates an unmonitored terminal node with no observed likelihood contribution. The BayesTools finite readout functions are reserved for sampler_probabilities. A distribution must be a normalized point mass at zero for every admissible parent value. Its marker is observed at zero. Use a distribution name prefixed with d<lowercased-module>_ for a provider listed in jags_modules, or use the BayesTools block marker dbt_block. Declare BayesTools blocks through one of sampler_joint or sampler_blocks. Use sampler_gates for model-verified gates, which take precedence over dbt_block when both mark a node. Supply package and module requirements through required_packages and jags_modules. The validated declaration is stored in the joint entry of attr(fit, "sampler_declarations"). Extensions reuse the compiled model text and data.

sampler_probabilities

optional character vector of sampled finite indicator node names or scalar indexed references in the compiled model. fit$sampler_probabilities gives one entry per requested indicator. The recorder can replace an active JAGS 5 base::Finite update for a full-rank scalar dbern or dcat with fixed integer support starting at 0 or 1, respectively. It preserves competing sampler assignments. Its entry is an mcmc.list with one row per retained draw in the same chain and iteration order as the model draws. The columns p[k] and log_p[k] are conditional probabilities and log probabilities at the indicator update in that iteration for support label k. The columns selected and lower give the sampled label and the lowest support label. Compiled aliases of one node return the same trace. An entry is NULL when no recorder was assigned to that node. A probability trace requires the same availability and support labels on every worker. Extensions append the corresponding rows. By default no probabilities are recorded. An incomplete or incompatible recording raises a BayesTools_sampler_probabilities_error backend condition.

sampler_nested_weights

logical. Share physical weight coordinates for eligible nested cumulative one-sided weights in a publication-bias mixture. The scientific priors and public weights are preserved. Unsupported pairs and mixtures whose private weight nodes are explicitly used or monitored keep their ordinary parameterization. The nested_weights entry in attr(fit, "sampler_declarations") records the two branch indices when sharing was used or the reason it was declined. Defaults to FALSE.

...

additional hidden arguments

fit

a 'BayesTools_fit' object (created by JAGS_fit() function) to be extended. A derived-draw view signals BayesTools_draws_view_sampling_unavailable, also BayesTools_sampling_unavailable and BayesTools_draws_view_unavailable, before runtime arguments are forced; extend its original_fit and regenerate it with JAGS_with_draws(). Fits without the parameter map and fit contract of this version of BayesTools (such as fits created by BayesTools 0.3.0) must be refitted: they stop with an error of class BayesTools_refit_required (see JAGS_validate_fit_contract()).

Value

A successful fit is a BayesTools_fit. It contains the sampled chains, model and data used for compilation, monitored nodes, and final per-chain parameter and RNG states. Extract the chains with coda::as.mcmc.list(fit). The sampler table fit$samplers is from the most recent successful backend run. For parallel fits it is the first worker's table. If worker assignments differ, fit$samplers_by_worker gives each worker's chains and samplers. A failed initial fit returns its error condition.

JAGS_extend() rebuilds the sampler from the stored states, adapts it for adapt iterations when needed, then appends draws without further burn-in. A saved and reloaded fit extends from the same state. Its extensions continue, as automatic fitting in JAGS_fit(), until every diagnostic that can be assessed meets the criteria of autofit_control after an extension, or until max_time or max_extend stops them. Within one call, automatic extensions continue the serial sampler. JASP fits also keep parallel worker samplers through progress updates and automatic extensions. Other parallel fits rebuild at each extension. The returned fit stores ordinary R data and can be serialized with saveRDS().

The adaptation attribute of a fit records the adaptation settings: initial, the adapt of JAGS_fit(), and extensions, a data frame with one row per backend extension (automatic extensions of JAGS_fit() and the extensions of JAGS_extend()) giving the adapt passed to the backend and whether the backend rebuilt the sampler, the only case in which it adapts. Warnings of the backend that adaptation was incomplete (class BayesTools_adaptation_incomplete, also BayesTools_fit_diagnostic) are issued and also kept in the fit's warnings attribute.

The burnin_check attribute of a fit records the readiness check between burn-in and sampling (see burnin_max_Rhat in autofit_control); it is NULL when the check did not run. It runs in the initial fit of JAGS_fit() only, afresh in each restart attempt, and not in JAGS_extend(), the automatic extensions after sampling, or a model without samplers. The record holds burnin_max_Rhat (the threshold used, a number also when it was "auto"), block (the iterations of the checked end of the requested burn-in), burnin_extend (in draws), thin (the thinning of the checked draws), blocks (one row per checked block, with the iterations sweeps it ran and its largest value Rhat and parameter), extension (the iterations added to burn-in), status ("ready", "not_ready", or "not_assessable" when no quantity could be assessed, which makes no claim of readiness and extends nothing), stop_reason ("ready", "max_extend", "max_time", "iteration_limit", "no_autofit", or "not_assessable"), and failing (the quantities of the last block above the threshold, with their values). fit$burnin is the burn-in that was run, and the iteration numbers of the draws and of sampler_probabilities count it.

See also

JAGS_check_convergence()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# simulate data
set.seed(1)
data <- list(
  x = rnorm(10),
  N = 10
)
data$x

# define priors
priors_list <- list(mu = prior("normal", list(0, 1)))

# define likelihood for the data
model_syntax <-
  "model{
    for(i in 1:N){
      x[i] ~ dnorm(mu, 1)
    }
  }"

# fit the models
fit <- JAGS_fit(model_syntax, data, priors_list)
} # }
